name: Nevada
overview: Nevada does not sell tax liens. When real property taxes go unpaid, the county tax receiver issues a certificate that lets the county treasurer hold the property as trustee for the State and county for 2 years after the first Monday in June of the year the certificate is dated, unless it is redeemed sooner. Interest is added to the unpaid taxes at 10 percent per annum, assessed monthly, until paid. If the property is not redeemed, the tax receiver deeds it to the county treasurer as trustee, and the board of county commissioners can direct the treasurer to sell it after giving notice of sale, so buyers at these auctions get the property itself.

counties.how_to_bid: Register online through the Treasurer's Real Property Tax Auction page or in person at the Treasurer's Office, with a $5,000.00 registration deposit per bidder in certified funds (cash, cashier's check, wire or money order). Registration is limited to 280 bidders. Only the registered bidder may bid, showing a bidder card; parcels are offered one at a time in the order of the published list. Pay in full at the Treasurer's Office by the stated time. There is no redemption period after the auction; properties are sold as is.

counties.how_to_bid: Based on the county's page for the last live auction: bidders register in advance at the Treasurer's Office in Tonopah or Pahrump with a $500 deposit in certified funds (cashier's check, money order or cash) and the Bidder Information form; there is no same-day registration and the bidder must be present. Bidders must be at least 18. The deposit applies to the purchase price for winners and is mailed back to others within seven business days. Payment in full, including the Real Property Transfer Tax, is due within a few days of the auction; there is no financing. Properties are sold as-is and all sales are final; the parcel list is published in the Pahrump Valley Times and Tonopah Times-Bonanza four weeks before the auction.

counties.how_to_bid: Bidders sign up at the Treasurer's Office at least fifteen minutes before the auction and get a bidder number; there is no charge. Mail-in bids with a cashier's check for the bid amount are accepted until 5 p.m. the last working day before the sale and become the opening bid if they meet the minimum. Payment in full (cash, debit or credit card with a 2.5% fee, money order or cashier's check) is due by 3 p.m. the next business day. Bids below the minimum bid, which includes the cost of the sale, may be refused. The sale does not guarantee title; a quitclaim deed is issued after recording.
